title: GIT-E composition identity: a committed git-composition record (content-tree bound) that badf_compose.py recomputes and compares; composition-verification subskill
objective: Make the composition claim a committed, machine-verified record. `badf_compose.py --record <path>` writes, after composing, a git-composition record: repository, target_ref, target_base_sha, source_ref, merge_base_sha, merge_method squash, expected_result_tree (informational), expected_content_tree (the composed tree with work/<WP>/ and badf/lockfile.json removed, computed on a temporary index -- the binding, which is what lets the record live inside the PR it verifies), policy_epoch, test_set_epoch null + non-coverage, suite_pattern, observed_at. Compose, in CI and locally, verifies a record found at work/<WP>/evidence/G07/composition-record.json on the composed tree: recorded target_base_sha must equal the base composed onto (else FAIL: stale record, recompute with --record), the recomputed expected_content_tree must equal the recorded one (else FAIL: content changed after the claim), merge_method must be squash and target_ref the default branch, and a malformed record is refused; no record is backward compatible (printed, not refused). The self-dossier indexes the record as `composition` evidence when it exists. The composition-verification subskill carries the author's order of operations and the rule: a rebase or a content change recomputes the record, never edits it.
business_value: SOURCE_HEAD_GREEN != INTEGRATION_SAFE is badf-git's core invariant, and the contract binds a nine-field composition identity -- yet CI computed all of it on every PR and recorded none of it; three rebases across GIT-B/C/D each silently invalidated composition. With the record, a moved base or a changed content tree is a compose REFUSAL naming the fix, and every landed change carries the content tree it was verified against -- GTGM v0.1 sections 10, 15 and 17 (GIT-E).
